665	    # brackets so a name containing a dot or a backslash can never be read
666	    # as a path separator: $["a.b"] is distinct from $.a.b.
667	    if name.isidentifier():

675	    The marker can never be a real key (see ``OVERFLOW_MARKER``), so a bare
676	    ``.*`` segment cannot be produced by ``_join`` for any real field name;

682	def _check_object(node: dict, record: dict, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
683	    if _is_collapsed(node):
684	        # A depth-capped node tracked no fields, so nothing inside the
685	        # record's value can be checked; the approximation is marked in
686	        # the schema instead of guessed about here.
687	        return
688	    fields = node["fields"]
689	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
690	    overflow_names = None if overflow is None else overflow.get("names")
691	    for name in record:
692	        if name not in fields:
693	            if overflow is not None and (
694	                overflow_names is None or name in overflow_names
695	            ):
696	                # Only names that really folded into the overflow entry are
697	                # checked against its widened type set; ``names is None``
698	                # marks a legacy overflow entry with unknown provenance. A
699	                # name never seen before is still unexpected.
700	                _check_value(overflow["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)
701	            else:
702	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: unexpected field")
703	    for name, entry in fields.items():
704	        if name not in record:
705	            if not entry["optional"]:
706	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: missing required field")
707	            continue
708	        _check_value(entry["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)

711	def _check_value(types: dict, value: Any, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
712	    kind = _kind_of(value)
713	    node = types.get(kind)
714	    if node is None:
715	        expected = ", ".join(sorted(types))
716	        reports.append(f"{path}: type {kind} not in field types [{expected}]")
717	        return
718	    if kind == "object":
719	        _check_object(node, value, path, reports)
720	    elif kind == "array":

725	# -- cross-revision compatibility -------------------------------------------
726	#
727	# Compatibility is read straight off the two committed schema trees, using
728	# exactly what ``check`` decides with: a record is accepted when every
729	# field it carries is a known (or genuinely overflow-folded) field whose
730	# value kind is in the entry's type set, every required field is present,
731	# and nested branches recurse. One symmetric walk therefore derives both
732	# directions at once: ``backward`` asks whether the new tree accepts every
733	# record the old tree accepts, ``forward`` the reverse.
734	#
735	# Each branch returns a ``(backward, forward)`` verdict pair. A branch
736	# either tree can only describe approximately - an overflow entry that may
737	# route the field, an entry flagged approximate, or a depth-capped subtree
738	# - is unknown in both directions and lists its source, in the same paths
739	# ``stats`` uses for approximated statistics (``$.*`` for an overflow
740	# entry, the subtree's own path for a collapsed node). The one exception
741	# is comparing a revision with itself: that revision is known to accept its
742	# own records, so ``Lens.compat`` answers compatible in both directions
743	# with no reasons after the revision has been read and validated.
744	
745	_COMPATIBLE = "compatible"
746	_BREAKING = "breaking"
747	_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
748	
749	# Witness recipe step tags (see ``_CompatDiffer``): an object field
750	# descent, one array-element nesting, a forced-kind leaf, and an omission
751	# of the innermost field.
752	_FIELD = "f"
753	_ARRAY = "a"
754	_KIND = "k"
755	_MISSING = "m"

758	def _combine_pair(pair: tuple[str, str], other: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
759	    return (_worst(pair[0], other[0]), _worst(pair[1], other[1]))

762	def _worst(left: str, right: str) -> str:
763	    """Aggregate branch verdicts for one direction.
764	
765	    A branch that demonstrably rejects a legal record settles the
766	    direction as breaking even when another branch is unknowable; without
767	    one of those an unknown branch degrades it to unknown.
768	    """
769	    if left == _BREAKING or right == _BREAKING:
770	        return _BREAKING
771	    if left == _UNKNOWN or right == _UNKNOWN:
772	        return _UNKNOWN
773	    return _COMPATIBLE

776	def _overflow_live(entry: dict) -> bool:
777	    """Whether an overflow entry can route a field name during check.
778	
779	    An entry with known but empty provenance routes nothing; an explicit
780	    ``names: None`` (a pre-tracking overflow entry) routes any name.
781	    """
782	    names = entry.get("names", [])
783	    return names is None or bool(names)

787	    if entry is None or not _overflow_live(entry):
788	        return False
789	    names = entry.get("names")
790	    return names is None or name in names

793	class _CompatDiffer:
794	    """Symmetric diff of two validated snapshots, aligned with ``check``."""

796	    def __init__(self) -> None:
797	        self.changes: list[dict] = []
798	        self.reasons: set[str] = set()
799	        # One deterministic witness recipe per breaking pair position. Each
800	        # recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object to that
801	        # position, so a record can be built straight from a schema tree
802	        # without matching change strings, re-deriving the alignment, or
803	        # risking a collision between a real field name and a step token:
804	        # ``("f", name)`` descends through an object field, ``("a",)``
805	        # through one array element nesting, and the terminal step is
806	        # either ``("k", kind)`` (force a value of that kind) or
807	        # ``("m",)`` (omit the innermost field).
808	        self.recipes: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
809	        self._steps: list[tuple] = []
810	
811	    @contextlib.contextmanager
812	    def _step(self, step: tuple) -> Iterator[None]:
813	        self._steps.append(step)
814	        try:
815	            yield
816	        finally:
817	            self._steps.pop()
818	
819	    def witness(self, direction: str, terminal: tuple) -> None:
820	        """Record a witness recipe for one breaking pair position.
821	
822	        ``direction`` names the accepting (record) side for the breaking
823	        direction being witnessed (``"old"`` for a backward-breaking
824	        position, ``"new"`` for a forward-breaking one); ``terminal`` is
825	        the recipe's terminal step. Every call site is a non-collapsed
826	        exact branch the accepting side demonstrably accepts.
827	        """
828	        self.recipes.append((direction, tuple(self._steps) + (terminal,)))

830	    def diff(self, old_root: dict, new_root: dict) -> dict:
831	        backward, forward = self.compare_object(old_root, new_root, "$")
832	        self.changes.sort(key=lambda change: (change["path"], change["change"]))
833	        return {
834	            "backward": backward,
835	            "forward": forward,
836	            "changes": self.changes,
837	            "unknown_reasons": sorted(self.reasons),
838	        }

840	    def change(self, path: str, category: str, breaking: bool) -> None:
841	        self.changes.append(
842	            {"path": path, "change": category, "breaking": breaking}
843	        )

845	    def compare_object(self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
846	        if _is_collapsed(old) or _is_collapsed(new):
847	            # A depth-capped object lets anything nested through check, so
848	            # neither direction can be settled field by field.
849	            self.reasons.add(path)
850	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
851	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
852	        old_fields = old["fields"]
853	        new_fields = new["fields"]
854	        old_overflow = old.get("overflow")
855	        new_overflow = new.get("overflow")
856	        for name in sorted(set(old_fields) | set(new_fields)):
857	            field_path = _join(path, name)
858	            old_entry = old_fields.get(name)
859	            new_entry = new_fields.get(name)
860	            if old_entry is not None and new_entry is not None:
861	                with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
862	                    pair = self.compare_entry(old_entry, new_entry, field_path)
863	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
864	            elif old_entry is not None:
865	                # The field disappears from the new exact fields. New check
866	                # only accepts it when the name really folded into the new
867	                # overflow entry, whose merged type set is approximate.
868	                if _overflow_routes(new_overflow, name):
869	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
870	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
871	                else:
872	                    # New check rejects records carrying it; old records
873	                    # omitting it additionally fail an old required field
874	                    # under the forward direction.
875	                    self.change(field_path, "field_removed", True)
876	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
877	                        # A legal new record omits it; the old
878	                        # required-field check reports it missing. That
879	                        # witness needs no value kind.
880	                        if not old_entry["optional"]:
881	                            self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
882	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(old_entry)
883	                        if kind is not None:
884	                            # A legal old record carries the field; new
885	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
886	                            self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
887	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
888	                        verdict,
889	                        (_BREAKING,
890	                         _BREAKING if not old_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE),
891	                    )
892	            else:
893	                # The field appears only among the new exact fields. Old
894	                # check accepts it only through its own overflow entry.
895	                if _overflow_routes(old_overflow, name):
896	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
897	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
898	                else:
899	                    # Backward: an old record omits it, so a new required
900	                    # field rejects that record while a new optional one
901	                    # lets it through. Forward: old check calls any record
902	                    # carrying it unexpected.
903	                    self.change(
904	                        field_path, "field_added", not new_entry["optional"]
905	                    )
906	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
907	                        # A legal old record omits it; the new
908	                        # required-field check reports it missing.
909	                        if not new_entry["optional"]:
910	                            self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
911	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(new_entry)
912	                        if kind is not None:
913	                            # A legal new record carries the field; old
914	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
915	                            self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
916	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
917	                        verdict,
918	                        (_BREAKING if not new_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE,
919	                         _BREAKING),
920	                    )
921	        # A live overflow entry on either side folds names whose accepted
922	        # branches cannot be attributed exactly; every branch it governs is
923	        # unknown both ways. The marker can never be a real field name.
924	        for entry in (old_overflow, new_overflow):
925	            if entry is not None and _overflow_live(entry):
926	                self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
927	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
928	        return verdict

930	    @staticmethod
931	    def _witness_present_kind(entry: dict) -> str | None:
932	        """Deterministic kind a legal record uses for this exact entry.
933	
934	        Exact field entries compared here are never approximate, and a
935	        validated entry has observed at least one record, so its type set
936	        is non-empty. The fixed kind order (null, boolean, number, string,
937	        array, object) makes the choice independent of dict iteration
938	        order; scalars are preferred and an array precedes an object.
939	        """
940	        for kind in _KINDS:
941	            if kind in entry["types"]:
942	                return kind
943	        return None

945	    def compare_entry(
946	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
947	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
948	        if old.get("approximate") or new.get("approximate"):
949	            # An entry flagged approximate absorbed overflow statistics in
950	            # an exact field position; its accepted value set cannot be
951	            # attributed precisely, so no change beneath it is asserted.
952	            self.reasons.add(path)
953	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
954	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
955	        if old["optional"] != new["optional"]:
956	            if old["optional"]:
957	                # Optional becomes required: old records may omit it. The
958	                # field name is the current innermost step; the missing
959	                # witness omits exactly that field.
960	                self.change(path, "optional_to_required", True)
961	                self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
962	                verdict = (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE)
963	            else:
964	                # Required becomes optional: new records may omit it.
965	                self.change(path, "required_to_optional", False)
966	                self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
967	                verdict = (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING)
968	        verdict = _combine_pair(
969	            verdict, self.compare_types(old["types"], new["types"], path, "type")
970	        )
971	        return verdict

973	    def compare_types(
974	        self, old_types: dict, new_types: dict, path: str, prefix: str
975	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
976	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
977	        for kind in _KINDS:
978	            if kind not in old_types and kind not in new_types:
979	                continue
980	            old_node = old_types.get(kind)
981	            new_node = new_types.get(kind)
982	            if old_node is not None and new_node is not None:
983	                verdict = _combine_pair(
984	                    verdict, self.compare_kind(old_node, new_node, path)
985	                )
986	            elif old_node is not None:
987	                # Records of this kind are legal on the old side but the
988	                # new type set no longer contains it (narrowing). A record
989	                # forcing exactly this kind is the backward witness.
990	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_removed", True)
991	                self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
992	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
993	            else:
994	                # The new side widened with this kind; old check rejects
995	                # new records that take it (forward breaking), while old
996	                # records still pass the new, wider check.
997	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_added", False)
998	                self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
999	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))

1002	    def compare_kind(
1003	        self, old_node: dict, new_node: dict, path: str
1004	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
1005	        kind = old_node["kind"]
1006	        if kind in ("null", "boolean", "number", "string"):
1007	            return _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
1008	        if kind == "object":
1009	            return self.compare_object(old_node, new_node, path)
1010	        return self.compare_arrays(old_node, new_node, path)

1012	    def compare_arrays(
1013	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
1014	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
1015	        """Compare array element branches under one schema-level path.
1016	
1017	        check walks every element against the single merged element type
1018	        set (a schema has no concrete indices), and it enforces that set
1019	        even for a depth-capped array - only a collapsed *child* hides
1020	        structure. So scalar element kinds gate exactly (rendered as
1021	        ``path[]``) and collapsed element objects taint beneath them;
1022	        element objects then join fields normally (``path[].name``). The
1023	        matching array-level step marks the one nesting level check
1024	        descends through per element.
1025	        """
1026	        element_path = f"{path}[]"
1027	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
1028	        for kind in _KINDS:
1029	            if kind not in old["elements"] and kind not in new["elements"]:
1030	                continue
1031	            old_child = old["elements"].get(kind)
1032	            new_child = new["elements"].get(kind)
1033	            if old_child is not None and new_child is not None:
1034	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
1035	                    pair = self.compare_kind(old_child, new_child, element_path)
1036	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
1037	            elif old_child is not None:
1038	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_removed", True)
1039	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
1040	                    self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
1041	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
1042	            else:
1043	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_added", False)
1044	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
1045	                    self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
1046	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))
1047	        return verdict

1057	# -- breaking-change witnesses ----------------------------------------------
1058	#
1059	# A witness for a breaking direction is one JSON object that the accepting
1060	# revision's ``check`` accepts (an empty report list) and the rejecting
1061	# revision's ``check`` rejects (the full, non-empty report list). The
1062	# differ records one recipe per breaking pair position while it walks; a
1063	# recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object, and the builder
1064	# below turns each into a concrete, deterministic record straight off the
1065	# accepting revision's tree - it never parses change strings and never
1066	# invents fields, kinds or values the accepting schema has not observed.
1067	# Required sibling fields are filled along the way so the record is legal
1068	# as a whole, not just at the breaking position; approximated branches are
1069	# never forced (a recipe can only end on a branch the differ proved), so
1070	# an ``unknown`` direction simply yields no witness.
1071	
1072	# Canonical, deterministic leaf values. Booleans and numbers stay
1073	# distinct kinds (``True`` is never used where a number is required), and
1074	# ``None`` is only produced for the explicit null kind, never for a
1075	# missing field.
1076	_WITNESS_VALUES = {
1077	    "null": None,
1078	    "boolean": True,
1079	    "number": 1,
1080	    "string": "x",
1081	}
1082	
1083	
1084	def _check_against(root: dict, record: Any) -> list[str]:
1085	    """Run the exact ``check`` pipeline against an in-memory root."""
1086	    reports: list[str] = []
1087	    if not isinstance(record, dict):
1088	        return [f"$: type {_kind_of(record)} not in field types [object]"]
1089	    _check_object(root, record, "$", reports)
1090	    return reports

1093	def _first_kind(types: dict) -> str | None:
1094	    for kind in _KINDS:
1095	        if kind in types:
1096	            return kind
1097	    return None

1100	def _complete_value(types: dict, kind: str) -> Any:
1101	    """A deterministic value of ``kind`` legal under ``types``.
1102	
1103	    Scalars use canonical values; an object carries every required field
1104	    (each filled the same way); an array carries one complete element (or
1105	    stays empty when the schema tracked no element kinds - an empty array
1106	    passes check whatever the element type set).
1107	    """
1108	    if kind in _WITNESS_VALUES:
1109	        return _WITNESS_VALUES[kind]
1110	    node = types[kind]
1111	    if kind == "object":
1112	        return _complete_object(node)
1113	    return _complete_array(node)
1114

1116	def _complete_object(node: dict) -> dict:
1117	    if _is_collapsed(node):
1118	        # A depth-capped object accepts anything, so the empty object is
1119	        # the smallest deterministic legal value.
1120	        return {}
1121	    record: dict[str, Any] = {}
1122	    for name in sorted(node["fields"]):
1123	        entry = node["fields"][name]
1124	        if entry["optional"]:
1125	            continue
1126	        kind = _first_kind(entry["types"])
1127	        if kind is not None:
1128	            record[name] = _complete_value(entry["types"], kind)
1129	    return record
1130	
1131	
1132	def _complete_array(node: dict) -> list:
1133	    kind = _first_kind(node["elements"])
1134	    if kind is None:
1135	        # No element kinds were ever observed (empty arrays folded here);
1136	        # check walks no elements, so the empty array passes.
1137	        return []
1138	    return [_complete_value(node["elements"], kind)]
1139

1141	def _fill_required(node: dict, record: dict, skip: str | None) -> None:
1142	    """Add every still-missing required sibling field to ``record``."""
1143	    if _is_collapsed(node):
1144	        return
1145	    for name in sorted(node["fields"]):
1146	        if name == skip or name in record:
1147	            continue
1148	        entry = node["fields"][name]
1149	        if entry["optional"]:
1150	            continue
1151	        kind = _first_kind(entry["types"])
1152	        if kind is not None:
1153	            record[name] = _complete_value(entry["types"], kind)

1156	def _witness_value(types: dict, recipe: tuple, index: int) -> tuple[Any, int]:
1157	    """Build the value at one field/element position from ``recipe``.
1158	
1159	    ``types`` is the accepting side's type set at that position and
1160	    ``index`` points at the next step. Returns the value and the index of
1161	    the consumed terminal step.
1162	    """
1163	    tag, *payload = recipe[index]
1164	    if tag == _ARRAY:
1165	        # One nesting level: check walks every element against the one
1166	        # merged element set, so a single element witnesses the branch.
1167	        node = types["array"]
1168	        element, terminal = _witness_value(node["elements"], recipe, index + 1)
1169	        return [element], terminal
1170	    if tag == _FIELD:
1171	        node = types["object"]
1172	        return _witness_object_field(node, recipe, index)
1173	    # Terminal forced kind.
1174	    assert tag == _KIND
1175	    return _complete_value(types, payload[0]), index
1176	
1177	
1178	def _witness_object_field(
1179	    node: dict, recipe: tuple, index: int
1180	) -> tuple[Any, int]:
1181	    """Build an object value, forcing the recipe's field within it."""
1182	    tag, name = recipe[index]
1183	    assert tag == _FIELD
1184	    record: dict[str, Any] = {}
1185	    next_index = index + 1
1186	    next_step = recipe[next_index]
1187	    if next_step[0] == _MISSING:
1188	        # The witness omits this field, which the accepting tree may not
1189	        # even track (a field the other side removed or only it requires);
1190	        # only required siblings are filled.
1191	        _fill_required(node, record, name)
1192	        return record, next_index
1193	    entry = node["fields"][name]
1194	    value, terminal = _witness_value(entry["types"], recipe, next_index)
1195	    record[name] = value
1196	    _fill_required(node, record, name)
1197	    return record, terminal
1198

1200	def _witness_record(root: dict, recipe: tuple) -> dict:
1201	    """Build the deterministic record one witness recipe describes."""
1202	    record, terminal = _witness_object_field(root, recipe, 0)
1203	    assert terminal == len(recipe) - 1
1204	    return record

1207	def _witness_report(
1208	    old_revision: int, new_revision: int, old_root: dict, new_root: dict
1209	) -> dict:
1210	    """The compat report plus verifiable breaking-direction witnesses."""
1211	    differ = _CompatDiffer()
1212	    report = differ.diff(old_root, new_root)
1213	    witnesses: dict[str, Any] = {"backward": None, "forward": None}
1214	    for direction, verdict, accepting, rejecting, side in (
1215	        ("backward", report["backward"], old_root, new_root, "old"),
1216	        ("forward", report["forward"], new_root, old_root, "new"),
1217	    ):
1218	        if verdict != _BREAKING:
1219	            # A compatible direction has no counterexample; an unknown
1220	            # direction cannot be settled, so one must never be forged.
1221	            continue
1222	        chosen: dict[str, Any] | None = None
1223	        for recipe_side, recipe in differ.recipes:
1224	            if recipe_side != side:
1225	                continue
1226	            record = _witness_record(accepting, recipe)
1227	            accepted_reports = _check_against(accepting, record)
1228	            rejected_reports = _check_against(rejecting, record)
1229	            if not accepted_reports and rejected_reports:
1230	                chosen = {"record": record, "reports": rejected_reports}
1231	                break
1232	        # Every breaking verdict comes from at least one exact breaking
1233	        # pair position, whose recipe must verify through check itself.
1234	        if chosen is None:  # pragma: no cover - construction invariant
1235	            raise SchemaConflict("could not construct a verifiable witness")
1236	        witnesses[direction] = chosen
1237	    return {
1238	        "from": old_revision,
1239	        "to": new_revision,
1240	        **report,
1241	        "witnesses": witnesses,
1242	    }

1245	# -- field migration preview -------------------------------------------------
1246	#
1247	# A migration rule is a small JSON object describing one field-level edit:
1248	# ``{"op": "rename", "path": [...], "to": name}`` moves a field's value to
1249	# a new sibling name, ``{"op": "drop", "path": [...]}`` removes a field,
1250	# and ``{"op": "default", "path": [...], "value": ...}`` fills a field that
1251	# is genuinely missing (a present ``null`` is a value and is kept). The
1252	# path is a non-empty array whose string segments are literal field names
1253	# (a name containing a dot names one field, never a descent) and whose
1254	# ``null`` segments select every element of the array at that position;
1255	# the last segment is always a string naming the field the op edits.
1256	# Rules apply in order, each to the result of the previous one. A parent
1257	# that is simply missing skips the rule for that branch - parents are
1258	# never created - while a string segment meeting a non-object or a null
1259	# segment meeting a non-array is a structural ``ValueError``, as is a
1260	# rename whose target field already exists.
1261	
1262	_MIGRATION_OPS = ("rename", "drop", "default")
1263	
1264	
1265	def _require_json_value(value: Any, what: str) -> None:
1266	    """Reject anything JSON cannot represent, recursing into containers."""
1267	    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int)):
1268	        return
1269	    if isinstance(value, float):
1270	        if math.isfinite(value):
1271	            return
1272	    elif isinstance(value, list):
1273	        for item in value:
1274	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1275	        return
1276	    elif isinstance(value, dict):
1277	        for key, item in value.items():
1278	            if not isinstance(key, str):
1279	                break
1280	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1281	        else:
1282	            return
1283	    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be a JSON value")
1284	
1285	
1286	def _parse_migration_rules(rules: Any, *, label: str = "migration rule") -> list[dict]:
1287	    """Validate the rule list structurally before anything is applied.
1288	
1289	    Every rule must be a JSON object carrying exactly the keys its op
1290	    needs - ``op`` and ``path`` for all three, ``to`` for rename,
1291	    ``value`` for default - with a non-empty path of string/null segments
1292	    ending in a string, a string rename target distinct from the source
1293	    field name, and a JSON default value. Anything else is a
1294	    ``ValueError`` raised before any revision is read or any rule runs.
1295	    ``label`` names the group in error messages so forward and rollback
1296	    rules are distinguishable in a roundtrip preview.
1297	    """
1298	    if not isinstance(rules, list):
1299	        raise ValueError(f"{label}s must be a JSON array")
1300	    for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
1301	        if not isinstance(rule, dict):
1302	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index} must be a JSON object")
1303	        op = rule.get("op")
1304	        if op not in _MIGRATION_OPS:
1305	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: unknown op {op!r}")
1306	        path = rule.get("path")
1307	        if (
1308	            not isinstance(path, list)
1309	            or not path
1310	            or any(
1311	                segment is not None and not isinstance(segment, str)
1312	                for segment in path
1313	            )
1314	            or not isinstance(path[-1], str)
1315	        ):
1316	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: invalid path")
1317	        expected = {"op", "path"}
1318	        if op == "rename":
1319	            expected.add("to")
1320	        elif op == "default":
1321	            expected.add("value")
1322	        if set(rule) != expected:
1323	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: invalid keys for {op}")
1324	        if op == "rename":
1325	            if not isinstance(rule["to"], str):
1326	                raise ValueError(
1327	                    f"{label} {index}: rename target must be a string"
1328	                )
1329	            if rule["to"] == path[-1]:
1330	                raise ValueError(
1331	                    f"{label} {index}: rename target equals the "
1332	                    "source field"
1333	                )
1334	        elif op == "default":
1335	            _require_json_value(rule["value"], f"{label} {index} value")
1336	    return rules
1337	
1338	
1339	def _migration_containers(record: dict, path: list) -> list:
1340	    """The containers the path's final segment applies to.
1341	
1342	    Navigates every segment but the last: a string segment descends into
1343	    the named field of an object (a missing field drops that branch
1344	    silently - parents are never created), a null segment spreads over
1345	    every element of an array (an empty array simply selects nothing).
1346	    A string segment meeting a non-object or a null segment meeting a
1347	    non-array is a structural ``ValueError``.
1348	    """
1349	    containers = [record]
1350	    for segment in path[:-1]:
1351	        following = []
1352	        for container in containers:
1353	            if segment is None:
1354	                if not isinstance(container, list):
1355	                    raise ValueError("null path segment requires an array")
1356	                following.extend(container)
1357	            else:
1358	                if not isinstance(container, dict):
1359	                    raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1360	                if segment in container:
1361	                    following.append(container[segment])
1362	        if not following:
1363	            return []
1364	        containers = following
1365	    return containers
1366

1368	def _apply_migration_rule(record: dict, rule: dict) -> None:
1369	    """Apply one already-validated rule to the working record in place."""
1370	    op = rule["op"]
1371	    last = rule["path"][-1]
1372	    for container in _migration_containers(record, rule["path"]):
1373	        if not isinstance(container, dict):
1374	            raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1375	        if op == "rename":
1376	            if last not in container:
1377	                continue
1378	            to = rule["to"]
1379	            if to in container:
1380	                raise ValueError(f"rename target {to!r} already exists")
1381	            # Rebuild in place so the field keeps its position under the
1382	            # new name and the same input always yields the same order.
1383	            renamed = [
1384	                (to if key == last else key, value)
1385	                for key, value in container.items()
1386	            ]
1387	            container.clear()
1388	            container.update(renamed)
1389	        elif op == "drop":
1390	            container.pop(last, None)
1391	        # default fills only a genuinely missing field; a present null is
1392	        # a value and is never replaced.
1393	        elif last not in container:
1394	            container[last] = copy.deepcopy(rule["value"])

1397	# -- rollback rehearsal ------------------------------------------------------
1398	#
1399	# After the forward migration preview succeeds, the rollback rules run on
1400	# the migrated record and the recovered object is checked against the old
1401	# revision and then compared structurally with the original record. The
1402	# comparison ignores object key order and compares objects key by key;
1403	# arrays of the same length compare element by element. A missing key
1404	# records that field's path; a type mismatch, an unequal array length or
1405	# unequal scalars record only the current position and never expand it.
1406	# Missing is distinct from null and booleans are distinct from numbers,
1407	# while ints and floats compare by numeric value. Paths reuse the check
1408	# field/array notation (``_join``) and are reported de-duplicated in
1409	# string order.
1410	
1411	
1412	def _json_kind(value: Any) -> str:
1413	    """The comparison kind, splitting booleans off from numbers."""
1414	    if value is None:
1415	        return "null"
1416	    if isinstance(value, bool):
1417	        return "boolean"
1418	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
1419	        return "number"
1420	    if isinstance(value, str):
1421	        return "string"
1422	    if isinstance(value, list):
1423	        return "array"
1424	    return "object"
1425	
1426	
1427	def _scalars_equal(left: Any, right: Any) -> bool:
1428	    """Scalar equality with ints and floats compared by numeric value."""
1429	    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):
1430	        return left is right
1431	    return left == right
1432	
1433	
1434	def _structural_differences(original: Any, recovered: Any, path: str) -> list[str]:
1435	    """Every path at which two JSON values differ, check path notation."""
1436	    left_kind = _json_kind(original)
1437	    right_kind = _json_kind(recovered)
1438	    if left_kind != right_kind:
1439	        # A type difference (missing vs null, boolean vs number included)
1440	        # is terminal at the current position.
1441	        return [path]
1442	    if left_kind == "object":
1443	        differences: list[str] = []
1444	        for name in sorted(set(original) | set(recovered)):
1445	            field_path = _join(path, name)
1446	            if name not in original or name not in recovered:
1447	                # A key one side lacks names exactly that field path.
1448	                differences.append(field_path)
1449	            else:
1450	                differences.extend(
1451	                    _structural_differences(
1452	                        original[name], recovered[name], field_path
1453	                    )
1454	                )
1455	        return differences
1456	    if left_kind == "array":
1457	        if len(original) != len(recovered):
1458	            return [path]
1459	        differences = []
1460	        for index, (left_element, right_element) in enumerate(
1461	            zip(original, recovered)
1462	        ):
1463	            differences.extend(
1464	                _structural_differences(
1465	                    left_element, right_element, f"{path}[{index}]"
1466	                )
1467	            )
1468	        return differences
1469	    if _scalars_equal(original, recovered):
1470	        return []
1471	    return [path]
1472	
1473	
1474	def _structural_diff_paths(original: dict, recovered: dict) -> list[str]:
1475	    return sorted(set(_structural_differences(original, recovered, "$")))

1482	# is built once from the two validated snapshots and deep-copied per

1484	# forward preview and the rollback rehearsal are pure functions of the
1485	# record, the two roots and the already-validated rule groups.

1490	) -> dict:

1493	        return {
1494	            "from": old_revision,
1495	            "to": new_revision,
1496	            "backward": _COMPATIBLE,
1497	            "forward": _COMPATIBLE,

1504	def _forward_migration(
1505	    base_report: dict,
1506	    record: dict,
1507	    old_root: dict,
1508	    new_root: dict,
1509	    parsed_rules: list[dict],
1510	) -> tuple[dict, dict | None]:
1511	    """Run the source-check/rules/target-check forward preview.
1512	
1513	    Returns a fresh report (the pair's compat report plus ``migration``)
1514	    and, only when the preview reaches ``"done"``, the migrated working
1515	    record. The only errors raised from here are structural ``ValueError``
1516	    encountered while rules run.
1517	    """
1518	    report = copy.deepcopy(base_report)
1519	    migrated = copy.deepcopy(record)
1520	    source_reports = _check_against(old_root, migrated)
1521	    if source_reports:
1522	        report["migration"] = {
1523	            "stage": "source",
1524	            "record": None,
1525	            "reports": source_reports,
1526	        }
1527	        return report, None
1528	    for rule in parsed_rules:
1529	        _apply_migration_rule(migrated, rule)
1530	    target_reports = _check_against(new_root, migrated)
1531	    if target_reports:
1532	        report["migration"] = {
1533	            "stage": "target",
1534	            "record": None,
1535	            "reports": target_reports,
1536	        }
1537	        return report, None
1538	    report["migration"] = {"stage": "done", "record": migrated, "reports": []}
1539	    return report, migrated

1541	
1542	def _migration_preview(
1543	    record: dict,
1544	    base_report: dict,
1545	    old_root: dict,
1546	    new_root: dict,
1547	    parsed_rules: list[dict],
1548	    parsed_rollback_rules: list[dict] | None,
1549	) -> dict:
1550	    """The complete one-record preview shared by all migration entry points.
1551	
1552	    With ``parsed_rollback_rules`` left as ``None`` the report is the
1553	    ``migrate`` report (no ``rollback`` key); with a list (an empty list
1554	    included) it is the ``migrate_roundtrip`` report. Every structural
1555	    problem a rule hits while it runs propagates as ``ValueError``.
1556	    """
1557	    report, migrated = _forward_migration(
1558	        base_report, record, old_root, new_root, parsed_rules
1559	    )
1560	    if parsed_rollback_rules is None:
1561	        return report
1562	    if report["migration"]["stage"] != "done":
1563	        report["rollback"] = None
1564	        return report
1565	    # The rollback works on its own copy so the forward migration record in
1566	    # the report stays the migrated object.
